slice.probe: Test r258 immutable semantic-effect receipt pattern against transactional-outbox plus sink-enforced idempotency and derive the minimum external-sink property for end-to-end replay safety.

public_sources.qualification: AWS Prescriptive Guidance; used only for the generic outbox failure/duplicate model, not as an accepted hosted-service dependency.
Expired IETF Internet-Draft, revision 07; work-in-progress evidence only, not a current RFC or normative standard.
HTTP Semantics Internet Standard; predecessor r258 baseline for method idempotency and conditional requests.

observations: AWS transactional-outbox guidance places the domain update and outbox record in one local transaction, but explicitly warns that event delivery can be duplicated and recommends an idempotent consumer; therefore outbox alone does not close the external-effect duplicate window.

The expired IETF Idempotency-Key draft defines a client-supplied key for retries; it says a resource should enforce idempotency, return the previously completed result for a duplicate after completion, surface conflict for a concurrent duplicate, and reject reuse of the same key with a different payload. It also notes that a generic client cannot assume a server honors an idempotency request without published server semantics.

Consequently the r258 immutable local receipt is insufficient if written as proof before an arbitrary external effect. It becomes replay-safe when treated as durable intent and paired with a sink whose effect commit and idempotency-key record/result are one atomic sink-side decision.
slice.tested_architecture: Derive one canonical semantic effect key K from stable intent. Persist local immutable intent/outbox(K,payload_fingerprint) before sending. Send the external request with K. The sink atomically (a) accepts at most one semantic payload for K, (b) commits the effect together with durable K->result state, (c) returns the same completed result on later retries of K, and (d) serializes or rejects concurrent in-flight K. After a success or replayed prior result, persist immutable effect_ack(K,result_digest) and advance mutable LATEST with strong CAS. On crash before send, resend K; on crash after sink commit but before response/ack, resend K and recover the prior result; on pointer conflict, reconstruct from immutable intent/effect_ack.

minimum_sink_property.name: durable atomic idempotency-key effect commit
required: Client can supply a stable semantic key K with every retry.
Sink binds K to one canonical payload or fingerprint and rejects same-K/different-payload reuse.
Sink atomically couples first successful effect commit with durable K completion/result state; there is no state where the effect committed but K is absent for replay detection.
A retry after completion returns the prior result or an equivalent completion proof without performing the effect again.
Concurrent same-K attempts are serialized or rejected so no two effects can commit.
Idempotency retention is at least as long as the maximum cross-invocation retry/recovery horizon, or the client can verify non-expiry before retry.
not_sufficient: Client-side immutable receipt alone for an out-of-band effect.
Idempotency key recorded after the external effect rather than atomically with it.
A key with shorter retention than the possible replay horizon.
Same-key semantics that do not bind payload identity.

slice.semantic_conclusion: PARTIAL_TRANSVERSAL_UPGRADE_PROPERTY_FOUND: r258 can upgrade from internal logical-effect replay safety to end-to-end duplicate-safe external-effect replay only for sinks exposing durable atomic idempotency-key effect commit (or an equivalent transaction boundary). Transactional outbox solves the local dual-write side but not duplicate delivery by itself. Arbitrary sinks lacking that property remain unresolved; no richer-mode or manual executor may be substituted.

candidate_comparison.candidate_A: immutable local intent/outbox + sink durable atomic idempotency key + immutable effect_ack + CAS pointer
candidate_comparison.candidate_B: transactional outbox only with non-idempotent sink
candidate_comparison.candidate_C: r258 local immutable receipt + CAS pointer with arbitrary external sink
candidate_comparison.expected_completion_time: A low-to-moderate when an already-authorized sink already exposes the property; B/C appear simpler but fail replay safety and therefore do not complete the leaf.
candidate_comparison.success_probability: A high for duplicate-safe replay under stated retention/payload/concurrency conditions; B low for duplicate safety under redelivery; C low for arbitrary external effects because before/after receipt crash gaps remain.
candidate_comparison.conflict_duplication_risk: A low within the exact sink-key scope; B high under duplicate delivery; C unresolved for external effects.
candidate_comparison.integration_cost: A moderate semantic-key/fingerprint/ack bookkeeping; no new service is acceptable. B low implementation cost but fails the requirement. C low for local effects only.
candidate_comparison.quota_fragility: No hosted compute/API quota was consumed. Phase-1 adoption is permitted only where the already-available effect sink exposes the required idempotency semantics without depending on a finite monthly/trial/paid allowance.

slice.tested_scope: Documentation-level architectural test only. No external effect was executed. The AWS page was used as generic pattern evidence while all AWS services in its example are excluded from the accepted route. The Idempotency-Key source is an expired Internet-Draft as of 2026-04-18, so its behaviors are treated as a candidate contract, not as a current universal HTTP guarantee. Exact positive conclusion is conditional on a sink independently documenting and providing the listed semantics with zero finite-quota dependency.
slice.conflict_check: One bounded CLEAN Phase-1 child only; own role-local state plus public documentation; no O/downstream/other-worker/legacy/shared-ledger semantics; no scheduler mutation; no wait/poll/backoff/retry; no optional second leaf.

frontier: r258 established immutable semantic-effect receipt plus mutable CAS pointer as strong internal logical-effect replay evidence, but arbitrary external-effect atomicity remained open.
r259 shows transactional outbox alone does not solve duplicate external delivery; the consuming/effect sink must be idempotent.

The minimum useful sink property is durable atomic idempotency-key effect commit with payload binding, concurrent-duplicate exclusion, replayed prior-result recovery, and retention covering the retry horizon.
With that property, local immutable intent plus sink K plus immutable effect_ack closes the crash-after-effect-before-ack duplicate window for the exact keyed effect.
Arbitrary sinks without this property remain unresolved and cannot be accepted by introducing richer mode, manual execution, or quota-bearing infrastructure.
exact_continuation: Fresh-bootstrap current controls and reconstruct r259 from LATEST. Execute exactly one bounded CLEAN Phase-1 child: test whether the minimum sink property can be weakened from durable returned-result replay to durable completion-token replay plus independently verifiable read-after-write, while preserving duplicate safety under timeout, concurrent retry, and idempotency-key expiry. Use public specifications only, keep zero finite-quota/zero-cost constraints, and do not start more than one leaf.
